commit.message:
fix(mcp): send MCP-Protocol-Version header and negotiate 2025-11-25

The Streamable HTTP transport never emitted the MCP-Protocol-Version header and the client pinned the stale 2025-03-26 revision. Spec-current servers (e.g. AWS Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with an outbound per-user OAuth target) discard the negotiated version and deny every tools/call with a generic internal error.

Bump the negotiated version to the current stable 2025-11-25 (MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION) and echo the negotiated version in the MCP-Protocol-Version header at the transport's single #fetch choke point, so it rides GET/POST/DELETE requests uniformly.

Fixes #8264

commit.message:
fix(acp): key steer admission on client-owned prompts, window the dialog promotion FIFO

P1: joinActiveTurn and the defer drain gate now key on a dedicated
client-prompt in-flight counter (#promptWithMessage brackets only) —
autonomous brackets (IRC wakes, idle injections, scheduler continuations,
agent-initiated turns) raise the general count but never this one, so a
steer can no longer be admitted into a run whose output the client has no
promptTurn for. The dispatch-live wake fires from the client prompt's own
agent.prompt claim (onClaimed in promptAgentWithIdleRetry, probed for a
sync-prefix rejection so a busy-retry behind an autonomous run never
reports that run as ours), and a parked steer keeps parking through
autonomous runs that end first.

P2: the steering-arrival promotion is now a sequence-windowed FIFO:
#fireSteeringArrival tags each admitted group, the permission gate
snapshots the count when it parks (steeringArrivalSeq), and its read
drains exactly the arrivals after that snapshot in admission order —
the first post-dialog admission stays first, and a steer that fired
before the dialog opened keeps its natural queue position instead of
riding the promotion.

commit.message:
fix(coding-agent): keep explicitly empty subagent fallback chains empty

A subagent whose role sets retry.fallbackChains to [] skipped installing its own chain, so a provider failure walked the default role's chain whenever the default role used the same model. Empty chains now install as 'no fallbacks' at spawn, for deferred singleton patterns, and on cold revival; unset chains still inherit the default.

fix(coding-agent): stop listing identity-less OAuth accounts as missing usage

collectUnreportedAccounts flagged an OAuth account with no email, account, project or org identity whenever its provider's reports carried an org: the org gate found no org-less candidate report and returned 'missing' before the identity-less check. Devin browser logins store only the session token, while the Devin usage report carries an org, so /usage showed a 'no usage data' row beside the account's own report. Such accounts cannot be attributed, so they are no longer claimed missing when their provider returned reports; identified accounts keep the org-gated attribution.

fix(coding-agent): keep background completions from resuming a user-stopped run

fix(acp): stop dropping session/request_cancel in dispatch, queue, and autonomous windows

A cancel arriving with no live client promptTurn was a silent no-op in
three windows:

- a prompt accepted on the wire whose turn slot does not exist yet
  (still queued behind another prompt, or inside the dispatch window)
  started streaming after the client believed it stopped the session;
- a cancel landing on a settled turn with an autonomous run still
  streaming (steer-triggered follow-up, IRC wake, scheduler turn) was
  dropped with no abort;
- a prompt queued behind a cancelled predecessor ran anyway.

prompt() now registers a cancellation carrier for every accepted prompt;
cancel() marks every live carrier, keeps the live-turn cleanup path, and
aborts an autonomous run with the same bound as cancel cleanup (closing
the session on timeout). The queue callback consumes the mark when the
turn slot is created and resolves the wire response cancelled without
starting the run.
chore: bump version to 18.12.4

fix(coding-agent): keep the default model entry beside a deferred pattern's retry role

Recording a deferred singleton's initial model only under its subagent retry role left no explicit default entry, so assistant messages from a runtime fallback overwrote models.default and a history-based resume restored the fallback instead of the primary. Write the default entry first and the retry role after it, as the task executor does.

Cover the empty inherited chain with a real deferred session: live retry chain keys and candidates come from the persisted role, and resume after a fallback answered still restores the primary. Rename the executor test's custom role to a neutral name.

fix(acp): complete steer admission ownership across preprocessing, validate steering blocks, prune arrival history

Round-3 review findings on #15885:

- Client ownership is now reserved by #prompt synchronously at
  submission, before any dispatch preprocessing await (maintenance
  wait, command expansion, image normalization), and released when the
  dispatched turn settles. A steer landing in the dispatch window parks
  and injects into the owning run instead of being declined, so the
  host never resubmits — whose session/prompt would implicitly cancel
  the still-dispatching prompt. Auto-continues and queued-hidden
  drains reach #promptWithMessage directly and no longer claim client
  ownership: they are autonomous and must not admit steers whose
  output would have no client forwarder.

- The post-preprocessing admission check in #queueUserMessage rechecks
  client ownership (not just general isStreaming): a steer whose owning
  turn settled while its own image normalization ran refuses instead of
  injecting into whatever autonomous wake took the agent.

- A pre-start cancelled prompt observes its cleanup barrier: an abort
  that hangs past the timeout closes the managed session instead of
  surfacing an unhandled rejection.

- _session/steering block validation now rejects a present non-string
  resource.mimeType (schema types it string, never null) and validates
  the resource_link optional fields mimeType/description (string|null)
  and size (number|null).

- Steering arrival history no longer retains one group per steer for
  sessions that rarely open a permission dialog: park snapshots are
  tracked while a gate is live, released on its read or dialog end, and
  #fireSteeringArrival prunes entries no live snapshot can still read.

- Changelogs restored from upstream with this PR's entries alone under
  [Unreleased], rewritten briefly; the previous merge had spliced them
  into the immutable 18.12.4 section alongside duplicated upstream
  entries.

fix(coding-agent): keep a subagent's own fallback chain after temporary model switches

Retry fallback hops, prewalk and context promotion record the ephemeral `fallback` role, including the switch back to the primary. The live retry role hint dropped out at that entry, so once a session had switched models, or was cold-revived from such a transcript, chain lookup preferred `default` over the subagent's own (possibly empty) chain again. The hint now skips ephemeral entries to the role the session was last assigned; resume and role cycling keep reading the latest entry.

test(coding-agent): drive the empty subagent fallback chain through a real provider error

The spawned-subagent regression test faked createAgentSession and only queried the chain helpers, so a regression in the retry fallback path itself could pass it. It now runs a real child through runSubprocess against mock providers: with the role's chain explicitly empty, a primary that keeps failing gets no fallback request and its error surfaces; with no role chain, the child recovers on default's fallback.

feat(ai): request OpenAI 12h prompt cache for GPT-5.6+ on long retention

GPT-5.6+ on the Responses API sizes cache lifetime via prompt_cache_options.ttl; the legacy prompt_cache_retention: "24h" field is ignored there. cacheRetention: "long" now sends ttl "12h" (implicit mode unless a promptCache policy is set), stops sending the 24h field to those models, and Chat Completions rejects the Responses-only 12h ttl.

commit.message:
feat(coding-agent): skip idle compaction on never-expiring Codex prompt caches

Logged-in Codex accounts keep prompt-cache entries with no TTL, so idle compaction only discarded a warm prefix and forced a cold read on the next turn. Adds the prompt-cache-persistent catalog axis (isPromptCachePersistent, first-party endpoint only) and declares it for openai-codex.
fix(tui): keep the hub sidebar from collapsing under wide body content in Tern

fix(acp): coalesce repeated cancels onto one cleanup barrier, gate dialog supersede on user steering

Round-4 review findings on #15885:

- cancel() treats a turn whose cleanup is still unwinding as in flight:
  a second session/cancel arriving after the wire turn settled but
  before #runCancelCleanup finished now reuses that barrier
  (#beginCancelCleanup is idempotent) instead of falling through to the
  autonomous-run branch, whose second, uncoalesced abort could reset or
  interrupt a replacement prompt that started after the first cleanup.

- The permission gate only classifies a dialog as superseded by USER
  steering. The loop-owned signal aborts once per run for any queued
  steering source (agent-authored asides, IRC interrupts included), so
  the gate now re-checks the arrival window at each loop abort and keeps
  the dialog open when no user steer landed; a second listener on the
  arrival channel covers the case where an agent-authored steer already
  spent the loop's single soft abort — the aborted loop signal is the
  interruptMode-policy proof, so a user steer admitted afterwards still
  supersedes. In wait mode the loop signal never aborts and both paths
  stay inert, preserving the policy. The bridge receives the derived
  user-steering signal, so the wire dialog is only cancelled for user
  steering.

- Direct Promise constructions replaced with Promise.withResolvers per
  the repo convention (cancel()'s timeout, the never-settling test
  fake).

+Compression is **re-encoding, not word deletion**. Filtering function words out of an English sentence leaves a damaged English sentence (`System design: efficient process incoming data, multiple sources`). Instead re-frame each claim in a register whose grammar is punctuation and layout — then the function words have no work left and drop out on their own.
+
+Target texts are load-bearing: tool descriptions, system prompts, skills. A model executes them cold, with no author present to disambiguate. Compression that forces a guess is a bug, not a saving.
+
+## Procedure
+
+0. **Density gate — check before touching anything.** Two signals, in order: (a) are articles and copulas already near-absent? (b) compress one representative section and measure the token delta. Already in this register (house-style prompt, tool doc, spec) or delta under ~10%? **STOP. Report that it is already dense and keep the original.** Bullet length alone is a weak signal — API literals and enumerations inflate it. Measured on a real house-style tool prompt: 853 → 778 tokens (8.8%), while that pass silently dropped a `NEVER assume …` rule, a throw condition, and a `full-res` detail. On already-dense text the remaining words *are* the payload, and the expected saving is smaller than the expected loss.
+1. **Split** the source into atomic claims: one definition, obligation, default, or fact each.
+2. **Inventory the payload first, before deleting anything.** List every load-bearing token: identifiers, error/exception names, throw conditions, defaults with their units, bounds, and every MUST/NEVER/PREFER line. Anything you then drop is a loss you declare deliberately rather than discover later.
+3. **Cut what the model already knows.** "JSON is a text format", "tests catch regressions" → delete. Keep only what is specific to this tool, repo, or domain.
+4. **Cut restatements.** Merge every duplicate of one rule into a single canonical line, placed where it is needed. Two statements of one rule with *different scope* are not duplicates.
+5. **Frame each claim** — definition · obligation · default · condition→consequence · enumeration · verdict. The frame picks the construction.
+6. **Hoist repeated qualifiers** into one scope line: three mentions of "relative to the repo root" → `All paths repo-relative.` once, up top.
+7. **Re-encode**, then run Verification.
+
+## Frames
+
+| frame | English | compressed |
+|---|---|---|
+| definition | "The `name` field is the stable launch identifier." | `name: stable launch id.` |
+| obligation | "You must call open before you can run code." | `MUST open before run.` |
+| default | "If no value is given, the timeout defaults to 30 seconds." | `Default 30s.` |
+| condition→consequence | "Because navigation re-renders the page, refs become stale, so you should snapshot again." | `Navigation invalidates refs → re-snapshot.` |
+| property chain | "z' is an integer because z divides x²+y², and it is positive because x²+y²>0." | `z' integer since z divides x²+y²; positive since x²+y²>0.` |
+| enumeration | "The action may be open, close, or run." | `action: open, close, run.` |
+| exclusion | "any triple that is neither (1,1,1) nor (1,1,2)" | `triple ≠ (1,1,1),(1,1,2)` |
+| verdict | "Claim A is true, and claim B is false as stated." | `A true; B false as stated.` |
+| precondition | "This requires that the branch has already been checked out." | `Requires prior checkout.` |

+- **Label frame** — `X: value` for "the X is / means / consists of". One colon per line, never nested.
+- **Subject elision across a run** — name the subject once, chain bare predicates: `Integer since …; positive since …; unique.`
+- **Asyndeton** — parallel items, no conjunction: `articles, copulas, expletives`.
+- **Scope declaration** — one line retypes everything after it: `All paths repo-relative.` · `Times in ms.` · `All congruences mod 4.`
+- **Lazy specification** — state only enough to decide: `3·13·34-1 big` (over the bound; exact value irrelevant). Name the bound somewhere the reader can see it.

+Punctuation carries the connective:

+The body compresses hard. The trigger does not.

 ## Testing Guidance
 
 Test the contract the system exposes — not the easiest internal detail to assert.
 
 - Every new test must defend one **concrete, externally observable contract**: behavior, output shape, state transition, error mapping, or a regression-prone parsing boundary. If you cannot name the contract, do not add the test.
+
+### Good vs. bad test filter
+
+- **Name the failure mode.** Every test MUST state what a consumer observes if it regresses. Cannot name one? NEVER add it.
+- **Good: transformation.** One fixture MAY prove parse/render/normalize/encode/resolve behavior when output is computed, not echoed.
+- **Good: branch or boundary.** Distinct inputs, empty values, malformed input, version/provider routing, and state transitions MUST prove distinct outcomes.
+- **Good: external contract.** Exact bytes/shape MAY be asserted when a provider, parser, protocol, or persisted consumer reads them.
+- **Good: precedence or negative contract.** Keep explicit `false`/override-wins assertions and required absence only when they prevent a documented leak, downgrade, 400, or incompatible wire field.
+- **Good: regression.** A repro MUST trigger the prior real failure path and assert the corrected observable result.
+- **Bad: static echo.** NEVER test a constructor/builder merely copied a fixture or baked constant into an in-memory config/metadata field.
+- **Bad: success passthrough.** NEVER assert `fn(x) === x` when `x` was already supplied/declared valid; assert a transform, rejection, or downstream effect instead.
+- **Bad: wording/defaults.** NEVER assert prompt/UI boilerplate, a default literal, object existence, non-empty output, or length growth without a consumer contract.
+- **Bad: duplicate rows.** Parameterized/loop rows MUST each cover a distinct branch, provider/model path, or consumer contract; delete same-path duplicates.
+- **Metadata exception.** Exact metadata, identity, ordering, or `undefined` MAY remain only when a downstream consumer depends on it and the test establishes branch, precedence, negative-contract, wire, or regression evidence.
+- **Termination exception.** For cyclic/large inputs, assert a bounded output, surfaced error, or state change; bare `not.toThrow()` is insufficient.
 - No placeholder tests, tautologies, or "the code ran" assertions (`expect(true).toBe(true)`, bare `not.toThrow()`, non-empty string checks, length-grew checks, "prompt exists" checks without semantic assertion).

 - Don't duplicate coverage across abstraction levels. If an integration test already proves the behavior, drop the narrower unit test that restates it through mocks.

+"""Repository rule generating the hermetic clang + ld64.lld macOS cc toolchain.
+
+Linux exec hosts cross-compile the darwin addons with this toolchain; mac hosts
+keep the host Xcode toolchain. Like @msvc_cc, the repo holds only cheap
+generated files — wrapper scripts and the cc_toolchain BUILD — so iterating on
+flags never invalidates the big @llvm_darwin_tools / @macos_sdk downloads.
+
+Wrappers derive every path from $0 (execroot-relative sibling repos), so they
+work from Bazel actions (cwd = execroot) and from build scripts, where
+rules_rust ${pwd}-expands CC/AR to absolute paths and cc-rs/cmake spawn the
+tools from other working directories:
+
+    bin/clang      clang --target=<arch>-apple-macos against @macos_sdk, linking
+    bin/clang++    through ld64.lld. -mlinker-version tells clang the linker
+                   speaks ld64's -platform_version; MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
+                   defaults the deployment target to the addon floor (12.0)
+                   for the rare invocation that passes no -mmacosx-version-min.
+    bin/ar         llvm-ar, or llvm-libtool-darwin for libtool-style arguments:
+                   Bazel's macOS archiver flags are libtool's (-static -o), and
+                   cc-rs drives $AR with ar's (cq, s). Named `ar` because
+                   rules_rust hides any archiver named *libtool* from build
+                   scripts.
+    bin/ranlib, bin/nm, bin/objcopy, bin/strip, bin/ld   LLVM equivalents.
+
+The feature/action config is rules_cc's own unix_cc_toolchain_config.bzl with
+target_libc = "macosx" (macOS features: libtool archiving, -mmacosx-version-min
+from --macos_minimum_os, -fobjc-link-runtime), copied into the repo exactly
+like @local_config_cc does; the flag lists mirror what @local_config_cc
+generates on mac hosts, so both hosts build the same addon.
+"""
+
+load(":sdk.bzl", "MACOS_SDK_DIR")
+
+_ARCHES = {
+    "arm64": {"cpu": "darwin_arm64", "triple": "arm64-apple-macos"},
+    "x86_64": {"cpu": "darwin_x86_64", "triple": "x86_64-apple-macos"},
+}
+
+_CLANG_WRAPPER = """\
+#!/bin/sh
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl. {tool} for {triple} against
+# the @macos_sdk SDK, linking with ld64.lld.
+set -eu
+execroot="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
+llvm="$execroot/external/{llvm}"
+MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET="${{MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET:-12.0}}"
+export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
+exec "$llvm/bin/{tool}" \\
+  --target={triple} \\
+  -isysroot "$execroot/external/{sdk}/{sdk_dir}" \\
+  -fuse-ld=lld \\
+  "--ld-path=$llvm/bin/ld64.lld" \\
+  -mlinker-version=907 \\
+  -Wno-unused-command-line-argument \\
+  "$@"
+"""
+
+_AR_WRAPPER = """\
+#!/bin/sh
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl. Static archiver: Bazel's
+# macOS archive action passes libtool arguments, cc-rs passes ar ones.
+set -eu
+execroot="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
+llvm="$execroot/external/{llvm}"
+case "${{1:-}}" in
+  -D|-static|-no_warning_for_no_symbols) exec "$llvm/bin/llvm-libtool-darwin" "$@" ;;
+esac
+exec "$llvm/bin/llvm-ar" "$@"
+"""
+
+_PASSTHROUGH_WRAPPER = """\
+#!/bin/sh
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl.
+set -eu
+execroot="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
+exec "$execroot/external/{llvm}/bin/{tool}" "$@"
+"""
+
+_NOP_WRAPPER = """\
+#!/bin/sh
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl. Placeholder for tools the
+# cross toolchain does not ship (gcov/objdump/dwp).
+exit 0
+"""
+
+_BUILD = """\
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:cc.bzl — hermetic clang + ld64.lld
+# cc toolchain for {triple} from linux exec hosts. The toolchain() targets
+# registering this live in //bazel/toolchains.
+
+load("@rules_cc//cc/toolchains:cc_toolchain.bzl", "cc_toolchain")
+load(":unix_cc_toolchain_config.bzl", "cc_toolchain_config")
+
+package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])
+
+filegroup(name = "empty")
+
+filegroup(
+    name = "all_files",
+    srcs = glob(["bin/*"]) + [
+        "@llvm_darwin_tools//:all",
+        "@macos_sdk//:cc",
+    ],
+)
+
+cc_toolchain_config(
+    name = "config",
+    abi_libc_version = "darwin",
+    abi_version = "darwin",
+    compile_flags = [
+        "-fstack-protector",
+        "-Wall",
+        "-Wthread-safety",
+        "-Wself-assign",
+        "-Wunused-but-set-parameter",
+        "-Wno-free-nonheap-object",
+        "-fcolor-diagnostics",
+        "-fno-omit-frame-pointer",
+    ],
+    compiler = "clang",
+    coverage_compile_flags = ["-fprofile-instr-generate", "-fcoverage-mapping"],
+    coverage_link_flags = ["-fprofile-instr-generate"],
+    cpu = "{cpu}",
+    cxx_builtin_include_directories = [
+        "external/{llvm}/lib/clang",
+        "external/{sdk}/{sdk_dir}/usr/include",
+        "external/{sdk}/{sdk_dir}/System/Library/Frameworks",
+        "external/{sdk}/{sdk_dir}/System/Library/SubFrameworks",
+    ],
+    cxx_flags = ["-std=c++17"],
+    dbg_compile_flags = ["-g"],
+    host_system_name = "local",
+    link_flags = ["-headerpad_max_install_names"],
+    link_libs = [
+        "-lc++",
+        "-lm",
+    ],
+    opt_compile_flags = [
+        "-g0",
+        "-O2",
+        "-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=1",
+        "-DNDEBUG",
+        "-ffunction-sections",
+        "-fdata-sections",
+    ],
+    opt_link_flags = ["-Wl,-dead_strip"],
+    target_libc = "macosx",
+    target_system_name = "{triple}",
+    tool_paths = {{
+        "ar": "bin/ar",
+        "cpp": "bin/clang",
+        "dwp": "bin/nop",
+        "gcc": "bin/clang",
+        "gcov": "bin/nop",
+        "ld": "bin/ld",
+        "nm": "bin/nm",
+        "objcopy": "bin/objcopy",
+        "objdump": "bin/nop",
+        "strip": "bin/strip",
+    }},
+    toolchain_identifier = "darwin_cross_{arch}",
+    unfiltered_compile_flags = [
+        "-no-canonical-prefixes",
+        "-Wno-builtin-macro-redefined",
+        "-D__DATE__=\\"redacted\\"",
+        "-D__TIMESTAMP__=\\"redacted\\"",
+        "-D__TIME__=\\"redacted\\"",
+    ],
+)
+
+cc_toolchain(
+    name = "cc_toolchain",
+    all_files = ":all_files",
+    ar_files = ":all_files",
+    as_files = ":all_files",
+    compiler_files = ":all_files",
+    dwp_files = ":empty",
+    linker_files = ":all_files",
+    objcopy_files = ":all_files",
+    strip_files = ":all_files",
+    supports_param_files = 1,
+    toolchain_config = ":config",
+    toolchain_identifier = "darwin_cross_{arch}",
+)
+"""
+
+def _darwin_cc_impl(rctx):
+    llvm = rctx.attr.llvm_repo.repo_name
+    sdk = rctx.attr.sdk_repo.repo_name
+    arch = rctx.attr.arch
+    t = _ARCHES[arch]

+    for tool in ("clang", "clang++"):

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Extracts one directory tree from an Apple flat package (.pkg) on any host.
+
+    extract_pkg.py <pkg> <member> <dest> [--exclude <subpath>]...
+
+Copies the payload entries under <member> (a path inside the package payload,
+e.g. Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX27.0.sdk) into <dest>,
+dropping the <member> prefix and every entry under an excluded <subpath>
+(relative to <member>). Regular files, directories and symlinks are supported;
+anything else fails the extraction. Symlinks to one of their own ancestors
+(Ruby.framework's `Headers/ruby/ruby -> .`) are dropped: they make the tree
+infinitely deep, and Bazel's glob fails on them.
+
+Used by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:sdk.bzl to unpack the macOS SDK from Apple's
+Command Line Tools package on Linux hosts, where neither `pkgutil` nor `xar`
+exists. Standard library only. The three nested formats:
+
+    xar     the .pkg container: a zlib-compressed XML table of contents
+            locating each member (here `Payload`) in the heap after it
+    pbzx    the Payload stream: 16-byte-framed chunks, each xz-compressed
+            or stored
+    cpio    the decoded stream: odc ("070707") entries, octal ASCII headers
+"""
+
+import lzma
+import os
+import shutil
+import stat
+import struct
+import sys
+import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
+import zlib
+
+_CHUNK = 1 << 20
+
+
+def _payload_span(pkg):
+    """Returns (offset, length, encoding) of the top-level `Payload` member."""
+    header = pkg.read(28)
+    magic, header_size, _version, toc_compressed, _toc_size = struct.unpack(">4sHHQQ", header[:24])
+    if magic != b"xar!":
+        raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: not a xar archive (Apple flat package)")
+    pkg.seek(header_size)
+    toc = ET.fromstring(zlib.decompress(pkg.read(toc_compressed)))
+    heap = header_size + toc_compressed
+    for entry in toc.find("toc").findall("file"):
+        if entry.findtext("name") == "Payload":
+            data = entry.find("data")
+            encoding = data.find("encoding").get("style")
+            return heap + int(data.findtext("offset")), int(data.findtext("length")), encoding
+    raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: package has no Payload member")
+
+
+def _pbzx_chunks(pkg, offset, length):
+    """Yields the decoded bytes of a pbzx stream stored at pkg[offset:offset+length]."""
+    pkg.seek(offset)
+    if pkg.read(4) != b"pbzx":
+        raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: Payload is not a pbzx stream")
+    (flags,) = struct.unpack(">Q", pkg.read(8))
+    end = offset + length
+    while flags & (1 << 24) and pkg.tell() < end:
+        flags, size = struct.unpack(">QQ", pkg.read(16))
+        chunk = pkg.read(size)
+        yield lzma.decompress(chunk) if chunk.startswith(b"\xfd7zXZ\x00") else chunk
+
+
+class _Stream:
+    """Sequential reader over an iterator of byte chunks."""
+
+    def __init__(self, chunks):
+        self._chunks = chunks
+        self._buf = bytearray()
+
+    def read(self, n):
+        while len(self._buf) < n:
+            chunk = next(self._chunks, None)
+            if chunk is None:
+                raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: truncated cpio stream")
+            self._buf += chunk
+        out = bytes(self._buf[:n])
+        del self._buf[:n]
+        return out
+
+    def copy(self, n, out):
+        while n:
+            if not self._buf:
+                chunk = next(self._chunks, None)
+                if chunk is None:
+                    raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: truncated cpio stream")
+                self._buf += chunk
+            take = min(n, len(self._buf), _CHUNK)
+            if out:
+                out.write(self._buf[:take])
+            del self._buf[:take]
+            n -= take
+
+
+def _cpio_entries(stream):
+    """Yields (name, mode, size) for each odc cpio entry; data follows each yield."""
+    while True:
+        header = stream.read(76)
+        if header[:6] != b"070707":
+            raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: unsupported cpio format (want odc 070707)")
+        mode = int(header[18:24], 8)
+        namesize = int(header[59:65], 8)
+        size = int(header[65:76], 8)
+        name = stream.read(namesize)[:-1].decode("utf-8")
+        if name == "TRAILER!!!":
+            return
+        yield name, mode, size
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    if len(argv) < 3:
+        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
+    pkg_path, member, dest = argv[0], argv[1].strip("/"), argv[2]
+    rest = argv[3:]
+    excludes = []
+    while rest:
+        if rest[0] != "--exclude" or len(rest) < 2:
+            raise SystemExit(__doc__)
+        excludes.append(rest[1].strip("/") + "/")
+        rest = rest[2:]
+    prefix = member + "/"
+    found = False
+    with open(pkg_path, "rb") as pkg:
+        offset, length, encoding = _payload_span(pkg)
+        if encoding != "application/octet-stream":
+            raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: unsupported Payload encoding " + encoding)
+        stream = _Stream(_pbzx_chunks(pkg, offset, length))
+        for name, mode, size in _cpio_entries(stream):
+            name = name[2:] if name.startswith("./") else name
+            rel = None
+            if name == member:
+                rel = ""
+            elif name.startswith(prefix):
+                rel = name[len(prefix):]
+            if rel is None or any((rel + "/").startswith(e) for e in excludes):
+                stream.copy(size, None)
+                continue
+            found = True
+            path = os.path.join(dest, rel)
+            kind = stat.S_IFMT(mode)
+            if kind == stat.S_IFDIR:
+                os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
+                stream.copy(size, None)
+            elif kind == stat.S_IFLNK:
+                link = stream.read(size).decode("utf-8")
+                target = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(rel), link))
+                if not os.path.isabs(link) and (target == "." or (rel + "/").startswith(target + "/")):
+                    continue
+                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+                os.symlink(link, path)
+            elif kind == stat.S_IFREG:
+                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+                with open(path, "wb") as out:
+                    stream.copy(size, out)
+                os.chmod(path, (mode & 0o777) | 0o644)
+            else:
+                raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: unsupported entry type for " + name)
+    if not found:
+        shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)
+        raise SystemExit("extract_pkg: package payload has no " + member)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main(sys.argv[1:])

+"""Repository rule materializing the macOS SDK from Apple's Command Line Tools.
+
+Downloads the newest-SDK package of the Command Line Tools for Xcode 27.0
+(`CLTools_macOSNMOS_SDK.pkg`) from Apple's software update CDN — the
+unauthenticated catalog `softwareupdate` installs the Command Line Tools from —
+and unpacks its MacOSX27.0.sdk with extract_pkg.py, so linux exec hosts get
+the SDK straight from Apple, the way @xwin_sysroot gets the MSVC CRT from
+Microsoft. Requires python3 on the exec host (standard library only).
+
+    MacOSX27.0.sdk/   the SDK, minus its man pages, Mac Catalyst support
+                      (System/iOSSupport) and Perl modules
+
+The package download (~70 MiB) is sha256-pinned, so it lands in Bazel's
+repository cache; extraction (~5 s) is a pure function of it, so the repo
+opts into the repo contents cache.
+
+Bumping: the catalog lists every Command Line Tools release; the product whose
+`.dist` names "Command Line Tools for Xcode <version>" carries the package.
+
+    curl -fsSL https://swscan.apple.com/content/catalogs/others/index-27-26-15-14-13-12-10.16-10.15-10.14-10.13-10.12-10.11-10.10-10.9-mountainlion-lion-snowleopard-leopard.merged-1.sucatalog \\
+      | grep -o 'https://swcdn[^<]*CLTools_macOSNMOS_SDK.pkg'
+
+Update _URL, _SHA256 and _SDK together (the SDK directory name is printed by
+extract_pkg.py's "no <member>" error when it changes).
+"""
+
+_URL = "https://swcdn.apple.com/content/downloads/58/48/082-83364-A_KCEBOO2NJS/0d2rj4y5ucjlkgcvqt6f6a4pergug5tu2b/CLTools_macOSNMOS_SDK.pkg"
+_SHA256 = "d55351824fd17742fd6e1e7a252fa1028698f32147ee48be9a6b75442bf30575"
+_SDK = "MacOSX27.0.sdk"
+_EXCLUDES = [
+    "System/iOSSupport",
+    "System/Library/Perl",
+    "usr/share/man",
+]
+
+_BUILD = """\
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/darwin:sdk.bzl — {sdk} from the Command Line
+# Tools package, for the linux-hosted darwin cc and Swift toolchains.
+
+package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])
+
+# The SDK's settings file; its directory is the SDK root.
+filegroup(
+    name = "settings",
+    srcs = ["{sdk}/SDKSettings.json"],
+)
+
+# Headers, .tbd stubs and frameworks: what C/ObjC compiles and links read.
+filegroup(
+    name = "cc",
+    srcs = glob(
+        ["{sdk}/**"],
+        exclude = ["{sdk}/usr/lib/swift/**"],
+        exclude_directories = 1,
+    ),
+)
+
+# The Swift standard library and overlay interfaces, for swiftc.
+filegroup(
+    name = "swift",
+    srcs = glob(["{sdk}/usr/lib/swift/**"], exclude_directories = 1),
+)
+"""
+
+def _macos_sdk_impl(rctx):
+    if not rctx.os.name.lower().startswith("linux"):
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/darwin: @macos_sdk is for linux exec hosts; mac hosts build darwin targets with Xcode")
+    python = rctx.which("python3")
+    if not python:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/darwin: python3 is required on the exec host to unpack the macOS SDK")
+    rctx.report_progress("Downloading the Command Line Tools macOS SDK package (~70 MiB, repository-cache backed)")
+    rctx.download(url = _URL, output = "sdk.pkg", sha256 = _SHA256)
+    rctx.report_progress("Unpacking " + _SDK)
+    extractor = rctx.path(Label("//bazel/toolchains/darwin:extract_pkg.py"))
+    rctx.watch(extractor)
+    args = [
+        python,
+        extractor,
+        "sdk.pkg",
+        "Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/" + _SDK,
+        _SDK,
+    ]
+    for exclude in _EXCLUDES:
+        args += ["--exclude", exclude]
+    result = rctx.execute(args, timeout = 600)
+    if result.return_code != 0:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/darwin: unpacking {} failed:\n{}{}".format(_SDK, result.stdout, result.stderr))
+    rctx.delete("sdk.pkg")
+    rctx.file("BUILD.bazel", _BUILD.format(sdk = _SDK), executable = False)
+    return rctx.repo_metadata(reproducible = True)
+
+macos_sdk_repository = repository_rule(
+    implementation = _macos_sdk_impl,
+    doc = "The macOS SDK unpacked from Apple's Command Line Tools package (linux exec hosts).",
+)
+
+MACOS_SDK_DIR = _SDK

+"""Repository rules fetching pruned LLVM release binaries for the cross toolchains.
+
+Each rule downloads the official LLVM release archive for the host that
+fetches the repo and prunes it to the `bin/` entries its toolchain wraps plus
+the clang builtin headers (lib/clang/<major>/include — immintrin.h & co). The
+pruned trees are a few hundred MiB instead of ~10 GiB.
+
+    llvm_msvc_tools_repository    LLVM 20.1.7, clang-cl / lld-link / llvm-lib /
+                                  llvm-rc for //bazel/toolchains/msvc (linux
+                                  and mac exec hosts)
+    llvm_darwin_tools_repository  LLVM 23.1.3, clang / ld64.lld / llvm-ar /
+                                  llvm-libtool-darwin for
+                                  //bazel/toolchains/darwin (linux exec hosts).
+                                  23.1.3 is the first release whose ld64.lld
+                                  reads the arm64e.x1 targets in the macOS 27
+                                  SDK's .tbd stubs (llvm/llvm-project#222721);
+                                  older ones reject libSystem.tbd outright.
+
+Archive downloads (~1.5-2 GiB) go through repository_ctx.download_and_extract
+with a pinned sha256, so they land in Bazel's content-addressed repository
+cache: re-fetches after `bazel clean --expunge` or a .bzl edit only pay
+extraction. Checksums are the official llvm-project release assets.
+"""
+
+def _host_key(rctx):
+    os_name = rctx.os.name.lower()
+    arch = rctx.os.arch.lower()
+    if os_name.startswith("linux"):
+        host_os = "linux"
+    elif os_name.startswith("mac") or os_name.startswith("darwin"):
+        host_os = "macos"
+    else:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/llvm.bzl: unsupported exec host OS: " + rctx.os.name)
+    if arch in ("amd64", "x86_64", "x64"):
+        host_cpu = "x64"
+    elif arch in ("aarch64", "arm64"):
+        host_cpu = "arm64"
+    else:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/llvm.bzl: unsupported exec host CPU: " + rctx.os.arch)
+    return host_os + "-" + host_cpu
+
+_BUILD = """\
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains:llvm.bzl — pruned LLVM {version} ({host} exec
+# host). Consumed by the //bazel/toolchains/{consumer} wrappers.
+
+package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])
+
+exports_files(glob(["bin/*"]))
+
+filegroup(
+    name = "bin",
+    srcs = glob(["bin/*"]),
+)
+
+filegroup(
+    name = "builtin_headers",
+    srcs = glob(["lib/clang/*/include/**"]),
+)
+
+filegroup(
+    name = "all",
+    srcs = [
+        ":bin",
+        ":builtin_headers",
+    ],
+)
+"""
+
+def _llvm_tools_impl(rctx):
+    key = _host_key(rctx)
+    dist = rctx.attr.dists.get(key)
+    if not dist:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/llvm.bzl: no pinned LLVM {} archive for {} hosts (the {} toolchain supports {})".format(
+            rctx.attr.version,
+            key,
+            rctx.attr.consumer,
+            ", ".join(rctx.attr.dists.keys()),
+        ))
+    suffix, sha256 = dist
+    prefix = "LLVM-{}-{}".format(rctx.attr.version, suffix)
+    rctx.report_progress("Downloading LLVM {} ({}, ~2 GiB, repository-cache backed)".format(rctx.attr.version, suffix))
+    rctx.download_and_extract(
+        url = "https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases/download/llvmorg-{}/{}.tar.xz".format(rctx.attr.version, prefix),
+        sha256 = sha256,
+        stripPrefix = prefix,
+    )
+
+    # Close the keep-set over symlink targets (clang-cl -> clang -> clang-20,
+    # ld64.lld -> lld, llvm-lib -> llvm-ar), then prune bin/.
+    keep = {name: None for name in rctx.attr.bins}
+    bin_dir = rctx.path("bin")
+    for name in rctx.attr.bins:
+        tool = bin_dir.get_child(name)
+        if tool.exists:
+            keep[tool.realpath.basename] = None
+    for entry in bin_dir.readdir():
+        if entry.basename not in keep:
+            rctx.delete(entry)
+
+    # Prune everything outside bin/ and lib/clang/<ver>/include.
+    for entry in rctx.path(".").readdir():
+        if entry.basename not in ("bin", "lib"):
+            rctx.delete(entry)
+    lib_dir = rctx.path("lib")
+    for entry in lib_dir.readdir():
+        if entry.basename != "clang":
+            rctx.delete(entry)
+    for verdir in lib_dir.get_child("clang").readdir():
+        for entry in verdir.readdir():
+            if entry.basename != "include":
+                rctx.delete(entry)
+
+    rctx.file("BUILD.bazel", _BUILD.format(version = rctx.attr.version, host = key, consumer = rctx.attr.consumer), executable = False)
+
+    # Opt into the repo contents cache: the fetch is a pure function of the
+    # pinned URL+sha256 and the deterministic prune above, and the ~172 s
+    # extraction of the 2 GiB archive was the single largest cost of every
+    # fresh output base on ephemeral CI pods (profiled: run 30510579596).
+    return rctx.repo_metadata(reproducible = True)
+
+def _llvm_tools_repository(consumer, version, dists, bins):
+    return repository_rule(
+        implementation = _llvm_tools_impl,
+        doc = "Pruned LLVM {} release binaries for the {} cross toolchain.".format(version, consumer),
+        attrs = {
+            "bins": attr.string_list(default = bins),
+            "consumer": attr.string(default = consumer),
+            # host key -> [release asset suffix, sha256]
+            "dists": attr.string_list_dict(default = dists),
+            "version": attr.string(default = version),
+        },
+    )
+
+llvm_msvc_tools_repository = _llvm_tools_repository(
+    consumer = "msvc",
+    version = "20.1.7",
+    dists = {
+        "linux-arm64": ["Linux-ARM64", "832f2802a29457dc758f56e26e98558c6cd0e45fcd07186f540cb6e7f4e59385"],
+        "linux-x64": ["Linux-X64", "8494c98a774051a40bfe1187a2d6442f4bc107598998bbe1673d9bb1572cfd6f"],
+        "macos-arm64": ["macOS-ARM64", "6aa75de00575ad0663183b00f00f39992ded611b5136e57649ace1e6a53c0d16"],
+        "macos-x64": ["macOS-X64", "ccf82ffe7e136ee49659cb57157856a7963d0950fac3d05aabba0db75bfba26f"],
+    },
+    bins = [
+        "clang",
+        "clang-cl",
+        "lld",
+        "lld-link",
+        "llvm-ar",
+        "llvm-lib",
+        "llvm-ml",
+        "llvm-mt",
+        "llvm-rc",
+    ],
+)
+
+llvm_darwin_tools_repository = _llvm_tools_repository(
+    consumer = "darwin",
+    version = "23.1.3",
+    dists = {
+        "linux-arm64": ["Linux-ARM64", "56d005e339c979a696ed6c244e6472e16f3b1371e48987a07e6145bda7ee0d03"],
+        "linux-x64": ["Linux-X64", "ca9fe385a5d9e2d88132dc0e23a00e9f87f38fa75f67207b5e457d208e71d013"],
+    },
+    bins = [
+        "clang",
+        "clang++",
+        "ld64.lld",
+        "lld",
+        "llvm-ar",
+        "llvm-libtool-darwin",
+        "llvm-nm",
+        "llvm-objcopy",
+        "llvm-ranlib",
+        "llvm-strip",
+    ],
+)

+"""Repository rule detecting the mac host's Swift toolchain for the Apple Foundation Models bridge.
+
+Runs `crates/pi-natives/src/applefm/build-bridge.sh detect` on the host and
+materializes the result for the mac exec host toolchain (//bazel/toolchains/swift:host)
+the `applefm_bridge` rule resolves; linux exec hosts use the pinned swift.org
+toolchain instead (linux.bzl):
+
+    toolchain.txt   "<swiftc>\\t<sdk>\\t<fingerprint>", empty when no Swift 6.4+
+                    toolchain with the macOS 27 SDK exists (the bridge is then
+                    an empty file, reported as not built)
+
+Caching: the fingerprint (compiler version + SDK build) is part of the
+bridge action's inputs, so action and remote caches never reuse a bridge built by a
+different toolchain, and an unchanged toolchain never recompiles. The rule
+re-runs when the selection env vars (tracked through `getenv`) or the watched
+compiler/SDK files change, and on `bazel fetch --configure`.
+"""
+
+_ENV = ["OMP_APPLEFM_SWIFTC", "SDKROOT", "DEVELOPER_DIR"]
+
+_CANDIDATE_SDK_SETTINGS = [
+    "/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/SDKSettings.plist",
+]
+
+def _watch_if_exists(rctx, path):
+    if path and rctx.path(path).exists:
+        rctx.watch(path)
+
+def _applefm_swift_repository_impl(rctx):
+    line = ""
+    if rctx.os.name.lower().startswith("mac"):
+        environment = {}
+        for name in _ENV:
+            value = rctx.getenv(name)
+            if value:
+                environment[name] = value
+        script = rctx.path(Label("//crates/pi-natives:src/applefm/build-bridge.sh"))
+        result = rctx.execute(["/bin/sh", str(script), "detect"], environment = environment)
+        if result.return_code == 0:
+            line = result.stdout.strip()
+        selected = rctx.execute(["/usr/bin/xcrun", "--sdk", "macosx", "--show-sdk-path"])
+        for settings in _CANDIDATE_SDK_SETTINGS + [selected.stdout.strip() + "/SDKSettings.plist"]:
+            _watch_if_exists(rctx, settings)
+
+    if line:
+        swiftc, sdk, _fingerprint = line.split("\t")
+        _watch_if_exists(rctx, swiftc)
+        _watch_if_exists(rctx, sdk + "/SDKSettings.plist")
+
+    rctx.file("toolchain.txt", line + ("\n" if line else ""))
+    rctx.file("BUILD.bazel", """\
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/swift:applefm.bzl.
+exports_files(["toolchain.txt"], visibility = ["//visibility:public"])
+""")
+
+applefm_swift_repository = repository_rule(
+    implementation = _applefm_swift_repository_impl,
+    configure = True,
+    doc = "Detects the Swift toolchain used to build the Apple Foundation Models bridge.",
+)

+"""Toolchain and rule building the Apple Foundation Models bridge dylib.
+
+`applefm_bridge` runs crates/pi-natives/src/applefm/build-bridge.sh with the
+toolchain resolved for `//bazel/toolchains/swift:toolchain_type`:
+
+    mac exec hosts    the host Xcode / Command Line Tools Swift that the
+                      @applefm_swift repository rule detected (toolchain.txt;
+                      empty when no Swift 6.4 with the macOS 27 SDK exists)
+    linux exec hosts  the pinned swift.org toolchain (@swift_linux), @macos_sdk
+                      and @llvm_darwin_tools' ld64.lld, all declared inputs
+
+Toolchains exist only for arm64 targets (Foundation Models needs Apple
+silicon); with none resolved the rule writes an empty file, which the addon
+reports as "bridge not built".
+"""
+
+def _applefm_toolchain_impl(ctx):
+    if ctx.file.toolchain_file:
+        return [platform_common.ToolchainInfo(args = [], files = depset([ctx.file.toolchain_file]), toolchain_file = ctx.file.toolchain_file)]
+    swiftc = ctx.executable.swiftc
+    sdk = ctx.file.sdk_settings.dirname
+    swift_root = swiftc.dirname.rsplit("/", 2)[0]  # <repo>/usr/bin/swiftc -> <repo>
+    args = [
+        swiftc.path,
+        sdk,
+        # See //bazel/toolchains/swift:linux.bzl for why each of these is needed.
+        "-resource-dir",
+        swift_root + "/darwin",
+        "-I",
+        sdk + "/usr/lib/swift/shims",
+        "-ld-path=" + ctx.file.ld.path,
+        "-Xclang-linker",
+        "-mlinker-version=907",
+    ]
+    return [platform_common.ToolchainInfo(args = args, files = depset(ctx.files.srcs), toolchain_file = None)]
+
+applefm_toolchain = rule(
+    implementation = _applefm_toolchain_impl,
+    doc = "A Swift toolchain able to build bridge.swift: either a detected host one (toolchain_file) or a hermetic one.",
+    attrs = {
+        "ld": attr.label(allow_single_file = True, cfg = "exec", doc = "ld64.lld the Swift driver links with."),
+        "sdk_settings": attr.label(allow_single_file = True, doc = "SDKSettings.json of the macOS SDK; its directory is the SDK."),
+        "srcs": attr.label_list(allow_files = True, cfg = "exec", doc = "Every file the compile and link read."),
+        "swiftc": attr.label(allow_single_file = True, cfg = "exec", executable = True),
+        "toolchain_file": attr.label(allow_single_file = True, doc = "@applefm_swift//:toolchain.txt (mac hosts)."),
+    },
+)
+
+_TOOLCHAIN_TYPE = "//bazel/toolchains/swift:toolchain_type"
+
+def _applefm_bridge_impl(ctx):
+    out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.attr.out)
+    toolchain = ctx.toolchains[_TOOLCHAIN_TYPE]
+    if not toolchain:
+        ctx.actions.write(out, "")
+        return [DefaultInfo(files = depset([out]))]
+    if toolchain.toolchain_file:
+        # "<swiftc>\t<sdk>\t<fingerprint>": the first two columns, or nothing.
+        command = '/bin/sh "$1" build "$2" arm64 $(cut -f1,2 "$3")'
+        arguments = [ctx.file.script.path, out.path, toolchain.toolchain_file.path]
+    else:
+        command = 'script=$1 out=$2; shift 2; exec /bin/sh "$script" build "$out" arm64 "$@"'
+        arguments = [ctx.file.script.path, out.path] + toolchain.args
+    ctx.actions.run_shell(
+        command = command,
+        arguments = arguments,
+        inputs = depset([ctx.file.script, ctx.file.src], transitive = [toolchain.files]),
+        outputs = [out],
+        mnemonic = "AppleFmBridge",
+        progress_message = "Building the Apple Foundation Models bridge %{output}",
+    )
+    return [DefaultInfo(files = depset([out]))]
+
+applefm_bridge = rule(
+    implementation = _applefm_bridge_impl,
+    doc = "The bridge.swift dylib the pi-natives addon embeds, or an empty file without a toolchain.",
+    attrs = {
+        "out": attr.string(mandatory = True),
+        "script": attr.label(mandatory = True, allow_single_file = [".sh"]),
+        "src": attr.label(mandatory = True, allow_single_file = [".swift"]),
+    },
+    toolchains = [config_common.toolchain_type(_TOOLCHAIN_TYPE, mandatory = False)],
+)

+"""Repository rule fetching the swift.org Linux toolchain that cross-compiles the bridge.
+
+Downloads the pinned Swift release for the linux host that fetches the repo
+(the Ubuntu 22.04 build: glibc 2.35, and it runs unchanged on 24.04) and prunes
+it to what `swiftc -emit-library` needs to compile and link
+crates/pi-natives/src/applefm/bridge.swift for arm64-apple-macos against
+@macos_sdk: swift-driver, swift-frontend, the clang it links through and the
+host Swift runtime and compiler libraries those load (~900 MiB of ~4 GiB).
+
+    darwin/clang   resource dir for darwin targets (-resource-dir darwin):
+                   only the clang builtin headers. The default resource dir
+                   (usr/lib/swift) also holds the Linux corelibs module maps
+                   (CoreFoundation, dispatch, os, Block), which shadow the
+                   SDK's frameworks once on the clang search path.
+
+The open-source compiler builds the SDK's .swiftinterface files as long as its
+version matches the one that generated them (Swift 6.4 for the macOS 27 SDK),
+but unlike Apple's it does not put <sdk>/usr/lib/swift/shims on the clang
+search path, so callers pass `-I <sdk>/usr/lib/swift/shims`; linking needs
+`-ld-path` to an ld64.lld that reads the SDK's stubs (@llvm_darwin_tools).
+
+Runtime dependencies on the host: libstdc++6, libsqlite3-0, libncurses6,
+libuuid1, zlib1g (present on the Ubuntu runner images).
+
+The ~1.1 GiB archive is sha256-pinned (repository cache) and the prune is
+deterministic, so the repo opts into the repo contents cache.
+"""
+
+_VERSION = "6.4.0"
+
+# host cpu -> (download dir suffix, archive suffix, sha256)
+_DISTS = {
+    "aarch64": ("ubuntu2204-aarch64", "ubuntu22.04-aarch64", "28c28acb2b91ed0e3beff5e6ba3695a785e645d9bd374adcaa3b7c2a901bc763"),
+    "x86_64": ("ubuntu2204", "ubuntu22.04", "bce85ea80f1471b85f39993f9285dbc798ec8e1eac5f677e24b2ac693856f9f8"),
+}
+
+_KEEP_BINS = ["clang", "swift-driver", "swift-frontend", "swiftc"]
+
+# usr/lib entries the compiler and driver do not load (debugger, SourceKit,
+# indexing, static/embedded stdlibs, package manager).
+_DROP_LIBS = [
+    "libIndexStore.so",
+    "libIndexStore.so.21.0",
+    "libLTO.so",
+    "libLTO.so.21.0",
+    "libSwiftSourceKitClientPlugin.so",
+    "libSwiftSourceKitPlugin.so",
+    "libclang.so",
+    "libclang.so.21.0",
+    "libclang.so.21.0.0",
+    "liblldb.so",
+    "liblldb.so.21.0",
+    "liblldb.so.21.0.0",
+    "libsourcekitdInProc.so",
+    "swift/FrameworkABIBaseline",
+    "swift/embedded",
+    "swift/migrator",
+    "swift/pm",
+    "swift_static",
+]
+
+_BUILD = """\
+# Generated by //bazel/toolchains/swift:linux.bzl — pruned Swift {version} for
+# the linux-hosted Apple Foundation Models bridge toolchain.
+
+package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])
+
+exports_files(["usr/bin/swiftc"])
+
+filegroup(
+    name = "all",
+    srcs = glob(["darwin/**", "usr/**"], exclude_directories = 1),
+)
+"""
+
+def _cpu(rctx):
+    arch = rctx.os.arch.lower()
+    if arch in ("amd64", "x86_64", "x64"):
+        return "x86_64"
+    if arch in ("aarch64", "arm64"):
+        return "aarch64"
+    fail("bazel/toolchains/swift: no Swift toolchain pinned for host CPU " + rctx.os.arch)
+
+def _swift_linux_impl(rctx):
+    if not rctx.os.name.lower().startswith("linux"):
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/swift: @swift_linux is for linux exec hosts; mac hosts use the Xcode toolchain (applefm.bzl)")
+    folder, suffix, sha256 = _DISTS[_cpu(rctx)]
+    prefix = "swift-{}-RELEASE-{}".format(_VERSION, suffix)
+    rctx.report_progress("Downloading Swift {} ({}, ~1.1 GiB, repository-cache backed)".format(_VERSION, suffix))
+    rctx.download_and_extract(
+        url = "https://download.swift.org/swift-{v}-release/{folder}/swift-{v}-RELEASE/{prefix}.tar.gz".format(
+            v = _VERSION,
+            folder = folder,
+            prefix = prefix,
+        ),
+        sha256 = sha256,
+        stripPrefix = prefix,
+    )
+
+    keep = {}
+    bin_dir = rctx.path("usr/bin")
+    for name in _KEEP_BINS:
+        tool = bin_dir.get_child(name)
+        if not tool.exists:
+            fail("bazel/toolchains/swift: Swift {} has no usr/bin/{}".format(_VERSION, name))
+        keep[name] = None
+        keep[tool.realpath.basename] = None
+    for entry in bin_dir.readdir():
+        if entry.basename not in keep:
+            rctx.delete(entry)
+    for name in _DROP_LIBS:
+        rctx.delete("usr/lib/" + name)
+    for entry in rctx.path("usr").readdir():
+        if entry.basename not in ("bin", "lib"):
+            rctx.delete(entry)
+
+    # usr/lib/swift/clang -> ../clang/<major>: the builtin headers alone.
+    # Relative, so the link survives the repo contents cache relocating the
+    # repo (rctx.symlink writes absolute targets).
+    result = rctx.execute(["/bin/sh", "-c", "mkdir darwin && ln -s ../usr/lib/swift/clang darwin/clang"])
+    if result.return_code != 0:
+        fail("bazel/toolchains/swift: creating the darwin resource dir failed: " + result.stderr)
+    rctx.file("BUILD.bazel", _BUILD.format(version = _VERSION), executable = False)
+    return rctx.repo_metadata(reproducible = True)
+
+swift_linux_repository = repository_rule(
+    implementation = _swift_linux_impl,
+    doc = "Pruned swift.org Linux toolchain for cross-compiling the Apple Foundation Models bridge.",
+)
